parts.label: (i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Substitute for $\mathbf r$ and expand the scalar product to obtain an equation in $\lambda$, e.g. $3(5+\lambda)+(-3-2\lambda)+(-1+\lambda)=5$ ($2\lambda=5-11$), or $3(4+\lambda)+(-5-2\lambda)+(-1+\lambda)=0$. Must attempt to deal with $\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$. [M1*]
Solve a linear equation for $\lambda$. [M1(dep*)]
Obtain $\lambda=-3$ and position vector $\mathbf r_A=2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-4\mathbf k$; accept coordinates. [A1] Total 3.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
State or imply a normal vector of $p$ is $3\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k$, or equivalent. [B1]
Use correct method to evaluate a scalar product of relevant vectors, e.g. $(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\mathbin{\cdot}(3\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k)$. [M1]
Using the correct process for moduli, divide the scalar product by their product and evaluate inverse sine or cosine; guidance displays $\cos\theta=2/(\sqrt6\sqrt{11})$. Second M1 is available if working with wrong vectors. [M1]
Obtain $14.3^\circ$ or 0.249 radians, or better. [A1]
Alternative 1: use a point on $l$ and $3x+y+z=5$ to find distance from the plane, e.g. $B(5,-3,-1)$ [M1]; $d=|3(5)-3-1-5|/\sqrt{9+1+1}=6/\sqrt{11}=1.809\ldots$ [A1]; complete method, e.g. $\sin\theta=d/AB$ [M1]; $\theta=\sin^{-1}(6/(\sqrt{11}\sqrt{54}))=0.249$ or better [A1].
Alternative 2: state normal $3\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k$ [B1]; evaluate vector product $(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\times(3\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k)$, guidance $3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+7\mathbf k$ [M1]; divide modulus by product of moduli and evaluate inverse sine or cosine, $\sin\theta=\sqrt{3^2+2^2+7^2}/(\sqrt{11}\sqrt6)$, second M1 available for wrong vectors [M1]; obtain $14.3^\circ$ or 0.249 radians, or better [A1]. Total 4. Printed anomaly: the official scheme displays $3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+7\mathbf k$; the stated vector product $(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\times(3\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k)$ evaluates to $-3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+7\mathbf k$, so the printed modulus is unaffected.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.answer: $\mathbf r=2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-4\mathbf k+\mu(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j-7\mathbf k)$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Taking direction vector $a\mathbf i+b\mathbf j+c\mathbf k$, state a relevant equation, e.g. $3a+b+c=0$. [B1]
State a second relevant equation, e.g. $a-2b+c=0$, and solve for one ratio, e.g. $a:b$. [M1]
Obtain $a:b:c=3:-2:-7$, or equivalent. [A1]
State $\mathbf r=2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-4\mathbf k+\mu(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j-7\mathbf k)$, or equivalent. Follow through on $\mathbf r_A$; requires “$\mathbf r=\ldots$”. [A1ft]
Alternative: attempt $(3\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\times(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)$ [M1]; obtain two correct components [A1]; obtain $3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j-7\mathbf k$ [A1]; state the same line equation, follow through on $\mathbf r_A$, requiring “$\mathbf r=\ldots$” [A1ft]. Total 4.
